samples.summary: The deliberate capture-phase listener registration is untestable by the suite as written — the overlay test uses a controlled, always-open Dialog, so reverting `addEventListener(..., true)` to bubble phase keeps every test green.
samples.evidence: image-viewer.tsx:143-165 registers the keydown listener with `capture: true` and documents the reason: "an overlay can only be recognised as open *before* Radix's own document-level handler unmounts it". The only overlay test (image-viewer.test.tsx:115-131) mounts `<Dialog open>` with no `onOpenChange`, so the dialog never unmounts on Esc — `hasOpenOverlay()` returns true regardless of whether the handler ran in capture or bubble phase. The test's own comment concedes this ("Controlled + always open ... it stays mounted"). Nothing in the file mounts an uncontrolled/dismissable dialog whose `data-state="open"` node is actually removed by Radix before the bubble-phase listener would fire, which is the exact production scenario (ShareDialog / mobile sidebar Sheet) the guard exists for. A grep of the test file for `capture` returns nothing.
searchedFor: checked file-detail.test.tsx and file-shell.test.tsx for any Esc-with-real-dialog test

samples.summary: Only one of the five branches of OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR is covered: `role="dialog"`. The alertdialog/menu/listbox entries and the popper-content entry are never exercised by any test.
samples.evidence: OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR (image-viewer.tsx:22-38) lists five selectors. image-viewer.test.tsx mounts only a Radix `Dialog` (role="dialog") for the positive case and a Tooltip for the negative case. No test mounts a DropdownMenu (`role="menu"`), Select (`role="listbox"`), AlertDialog, or a non-tooltip popper content, so those four selector entries could be deleted or mistyped and the suite stays green. Likewise the comment's claim that the guard "disarms ... as soon as a real overlay starts closing" (i.e. `data-state="closed"` during exit animation) has no test.

samples.summary: No test presses Escape against the real ImageViewer inside the real layout: the integration test mocks the viewer away, and the viewer test injects a mock onClose, so nothing asserts the end-to-end Esc→navigate path.
samples.evidence: file-detail.test.tsx:72-77 replaces `@/app/files/image-viewer` with a stub button, so the test named "hands the viewer the same destination for Esc" (line 131) never dispatches an Escape key at all — it clicks a stub. image-viewer.test.tsx asserts `onClose` was called, i.e. only that a mock was invoked. The composition is covered at unit level in two halves, but a regression such as the real viewer's Esc branch being guarded out inside the real header (e.g. focus landing on the rename input) would not be caught. Acceptable as a seam, but worth noting as the one behaviour the diff exists for.

samples.summary: The redirect tests assert only the eventual location via waitFor, so a transient redirect to the wrong path (before the workspaces query resolves) would still pass.
samples.evidence: FileShell's effect (file-shell.tsx:64-69) depends on `documentsPath`, which is `/documents` until `fetchWorkspaces` resolves and `/w/first` afterwards; the effect re-runs on the change, so a first, wrong `navigate("/documents", {replace:true})` is immediately followed by the right one. The test at file-shell.test.tsx:105-113 only waits for the final `textContent` to be `/w/first`, so it cannot distinguish "redirected correctly once" from "redirected twice, first to the wrong list". No spy on navigate/history entries is asserted.

samples.summary: `expect(navigate).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` in the share-link test is vacuous — no navigation-triggering key is pressed and both queries are disabled by `token`.
samples.evidence: image-viewer.test.tsx:163-173 renders with `token` (which sets `enabled: !token` false on both queries, image-viewer.tsx:100/116, so `prevId`/`nextId` are always undefined) and dispatches only `Escape`. `navigate` could therefore never have been called regardless of the code under test. The meaningful assertion in this test is the `window` `error` listener, which does detect the missing `&& onClose` guard; the navigate assertion adds nothing.

samples.summary: Test titled "falls back to the first workspace for an unknown workspace" passes `undefined`, not an unknown id — the named case is not the case exercised.
samples.evidence: use-documents-path.test.tsx:34-40 calls `useDocumentsPath(undefined)` under the title "unknown workspace". Both take the same `.find(...) ?? workspaces[0]` branch in use-documents-path.ts:19-21, so coverage is equivalent, but the title misdescribes the input; a caller reading the suite would believe the id-not-in-list case is asserted explicitly.

samples.summary: The headerLeading test asserts only `closest("header")`, not that the slot renders left of the title, so a misplaced slot (e.g. moved into the actions group) would still pass this test.
samples.evidence: file-shell.test.tsx:95-97 asserts `slot.closest("header")` is truthy. site-header.tsx renders both `{leading}` (line 55) and `{children}` (line 95) inside the same `<header>`, so the assertion holds for either placement. The positional check only exists in file-detail.test.tsx:117-120, not in the FileShell/SiteHeader-level test that owns the slot contract.
searchedFor: grep for a dedicated site-header test under packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/

verdict.reason: The claim checks out. image-viewer.tsx:163 registers the keydown handler in capture phase deliberately (comment at 143-145: the overlay must be seen as open before Radix's document-level handler unmounts it). The only overlay test (image-viewer.test.tsx:115-131) uses the fixture at lines 67-73, `<Dialog open>` with no `onOpenChange` — a controlled, never-unmounting dialog, as the fixture's own comment (62-66) concedes. Esc dispatched on that dialog bubbles to window with `data-state="open"` still in the DOM, so `hasOpenOverlay()` (image-viewer.tsx:40-42) returns true in either phase; reverting `addEventListener(..., true)` to bubble phase would not fail this test. The other tests dispatch on `window` itself (lines 97, 143, 158, 172), where capture and bubble both fire at-target, so they cannot discriminate either. I searched repo-wide for another exercise of the component: `ImageViewer` is referenced only in file-detail.tsx, shared-document.tsx, image-viewer.tsx and the two test files, and file-detail.test.tsx:81-88 mocks the viewer out entirely. No test anywhere references `hasOpenOverlay`/`OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR` besides image-viewer.test.tsx, there are no Playwright/e2e specs or hunt-oracle scenarios touching the image viewer, and no test spies on `addEventListener` to assert the capture flag. So the exact production scenario the guard exists for — an uncontrolled dismissable overlay Radix removes on Esc — has no coverage, and the test named "ignores Esc that dismisses an overlay layered over it" never actually dismisses an overlay. That is a real missing-test gap on the mechanism that makes the fix work, blocking under the test-adequacy rubric.
